name: Taylor Swift
hook: A country songwriter who sent Nashville demo tapes of Dolly Parton covers at 11, moved to pop on Madonna's model, and re-recorded her first albums when someone else bought her masters.
blurb: Taylor Swift was born in West Reading, Pennsylvania, on 13 December 1989. At 11 she went to Nashville with her mother and handed record companies demo tapes of herself singing Dolly Parton and Dixie Chicks songs. They all said no, so she concentrated on writing her own. At 14 she became the youngest songwriter ever signed by her publishing company, Sony/ATV. After a showcase at Nashville's Bluebird Cafe in November 2004, Scott Borchetta signed her at 15 to his new label, Big Machine, on condition that she wrote her own albums. She began as a country singer, and 'Taylor Swift' (2006) and 'Fearless' (2008) crossed from country to pop radio. For '1989' (2014), made with Max Martin and Shellback, she moved fully to pop inspired by 1980s synth-pop, naming Phil Collins, Annie Lennox, Peter Gabriel and Madonna. She signed to Republic in 2018 on terms that let her own her new recordings. In 2019 the music manager Scooter Braun bought Big Machine, including the original recordings of her first six albums. She said she was only offered them back if she earned each one with a new album, and refused. From November 2020 she recorded the albums again as 'Taylor's Version', so she would control how they are licensed, and in May 2025 she bought the originals back from Shamrock Holdings, which had bought them from Braun in 2020. Beyoncé's Wikipedia article records Swift calling her a major influence for showing artists how to push back against how the industry usually works.

signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Written alone as a teenager: she became the youngest person to write and sing a number-one country single by herself.

signatureTracks.title: Shake It Off
